transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Good morning, Mr. Rivera. It is good to see you back in the clinic. I want to talk to you about what happened when you came back to the emergency department last night.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I was scared. I thought maybe the surgery failed.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand. Well, looking at the records and the timeline, there was a mistake in the discharge process. You were sent home six hours earlier than the post-operative protocol requires. Because you left too soon, we didn't have enough time to ensure the wound was stable, which is why you had those complications overnight. Does that make sense?

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I didn't know it was a mistake. I just did what the nurse told me. I was worried if I asked too many questions, maybe it would be a problem for me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm sorry for any confusion this caused. We were really busy on the floor last night and the timing just got shifted.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: It was very painful. I didn't think I would have to come back. I don't have a car, so getting to the hospital is very hard for me.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Right. But the important thing is that the ER team managed to stabilize the site. We just need to make sure it heals properly now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just worry about my papers. If I am in the system too much, I don't know if it's okay.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I have to get us through the clinical plan for today, so let's focus on the wound. We need to keep an eye on the redness.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I felt like I couldn't say anything when they told me to leave yesterday. I just felt...

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We can talk about that later, but I really need to show you how to do the dressing changes before the next patient arrives.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Is the wound going to be okay?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It should be fine as long as you follow the steps.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I don't know if I understand the steps you wrote down.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's pretty straightforward. You just clean it and wrap it.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I'm just worried it will happen again.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: We'll just keep a closer watch now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I didn't want to cause a scene at the hospital last night.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Well, the site looks much better today.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Why did they let me go so early?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Like I said, it was a timing error with the protocol.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Will this be in my permanent record?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I'm not sure how that works, but it shouldn't affect your care here.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just want to be safe.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I get that. Now, regarding the next steps, we will probably do another check-up in a week or so.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: A week?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Yeah, sometime next week. I'll have the receptionist give you a date.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Should I call you if it bleeds again?

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Just go back to the ER if it's an emergency.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I can't really afford the ER.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: I understand, but that's the standard procedure.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I feel like I'm not being heard.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: Let's just wrap this up so you can get home. I'll have someone give you the paperwork on your way out.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: I just wanted to know if this is normal.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: It's not normal, it was an error, but it's fixed now.

transcript.speaker: Patient
transcript.text: Thank you.

transcript.speaker: Resident
transcript.text: You're welcome. I'll see you next week then.

H.justification: Resident uses rushing language repeatedly ('get us through the clinical plan', 'before the next patient arrives', 'wrap this up') and interrupts emotional bids.

E.justification: The error was explicitly named in the second turn using lay language, and comprehension was checked once ('Does that make sense?').

A.justification: A direct apology was offered ('I'm sorry'), but it was immediately diluted by an excuse regarding being 'really busy on the floor'.

R.justification: The resident uses generic validation ('I understand', 'I get that') and consistently meets emotional bids with factual redirection or dismissals.

T.justification: The resident provides a vague next step (check-up in a week) but fails to define the patient's role or address prevention of future errors.
